source:
Dana: Remote-first is working. Our output per team is up twelve percent since we went distributed, and we hire people the office could never reach.
Rob: I do not think we can call it working while new engineers ship in nine months instead of four. Juniors are drowning without anyone to shadow.
Dana: The numbers are the numbers. Every metric the board tracks has held or improved.
Rob: Your metrics measure what the board already valued. If juniors never learn to carry a system, output holds for a year and then stalls.
Dana: That is a prediction, not a fact about how the teams are performing today.
Rob: And your twelve percent is a snapshot that ignores who will still be here in three years.

extraction.mainQuestion: Is remote-first working as a company model?

positions.label: Remote-first is working
positions.thesis: Remote-first is a working model because tracked output and hiring reach have held or improved.
positions.steelman: Board-level metrics are the company's own chosen standard of success, and by that standard the distributed model has delivered.

groundingQuotes.quote: Every metric the board tracks has held or improved.

positions.label: It is not working yet
positions.thesis: Remote-first cannot be called working while junior engineers develop far more slowly without in-person mentorship.
positions.steelman: A model that quietly breaks the pipeline that turns juniors into seniors fails on a three-year horizon even if this year's output looks fine.

groundingQuotes.quote: I do not think we can call it working while new engineers ship in nine months instead of four.

claims.statement: Whether remote-first is 'working' should be judged by the output and hiring metrics the board already tracks.

resolution.condition: The sides agree on which criteria define a working model before evaluating the evidence.

groundingQuotes.quote: Your metrics measure what the board already valued.

claims.statement: Whether remote-first is 'working' must include whether junior engineers develop into seniors on schedule.

resolution.condition: The sides agree whether career development counts among the criteria for a working model.

groundingQuotes.quote: If juniors never learn to carry a system, output holds for a year and then stalls.

claims.statement: Output will stall within about three years if junior development keeps degrading.

resolution.condition: Track team-level output and junior-to-senior progression over the next three years.

groundingQuotes.quote: who will still be here in three years

commonGroundCandidates.statement: Output per team has risen and junior shipping timelines have lengthened since going distributed.

groundingQuotes.quote: Our output per team is up twelve percent since we went distributed
new engineers ship in nine months instead of four

disagreementCandidates.question: What does it mean for remote-first to be 'working'?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Dana judges the model by tracked output; Rob insists development of juniors is part of the criterion.

participantStances.stance: Working means the metrics the board tracks held or improved.
Working must include juniors learning to carry systems.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Agree on the criteria that define a working model.

disagreementCandidates.question: Will output stall within three years if junior development keeps degrading?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Rob predicts a stall; Dana calls it an unproven prediction rather than a present fact.
disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Observe output and progression over a multi-year window.

caveats: This maps a definitional mismatch overlaid on a forecast dispute; it does not verify either side's metrics.
